PROC MEANS: log, listing and HTML output

Source: vignettes/articles/guide-proc-means.Rmd
guide-proc-means.Rmd
library(sasonr)

A procedure step has three outputs in sasonr while the HTML destination is open:

  • the log: the program lines with the NOTEs of each step;
  • the listing: the procedure output as text, laid out at LINESIZE;
  • the HTML document: the same tables with the blue-and-grey style of the HTML destination.

PROC MEANS builds its output once, as ODS tables (sasonr_ods_table); the listing and the HTML document are both rendered from these tables, so they always show the same numbers. This article uses one small invented data set throughout.

The program 

res <- sas_run("
data trial;
  input arm $ visit week aval;
  datalines;
A 1 0 10.2
A 1 4 11.8
A 2 0 9.6
A 2 4 12.1
B 1 0 10.9
B 1 4 10.4
B 2 0 11.3
B 2 4 9.8
;
run;

title 'Change from baseline';
proc means data=trial n mean std min max maxdec=2;
  class arm week;
  var aval;
run;
")

The log

sas_log() gives the program lines with their numbers and the NOTEs of each step:

sas_log(res)
#> 1          
#> 2          data trial;
#> 3            input arm $ visit week aval;
#> 4            datalines;
#> 
#> NOTE: The data set WORK.TRIAL has 8 observations and 4 variables.
#> 13         ;
#> 14         run;
#> 15         
#> 16         title 'Change from baseline';
#> 17         proc means data=trial n mean std min max maxdec=2;
#> 18           class arm week;
#> 19           var aval;
#> 20         run;
#> 
#> NOTE: There were 8 observations read from the data set WORK.TRIAL.

sas_log(res, echo = FALSE) keeps only the messages; in a terminal with colours, print(res) shows NOTEs in blue, WARNINGs in green and ERRORs in red. The same log as HTML:

The listing

$listing holds the procedure output as text, with the title, the procedure title, the CLASS columns and the statistic columns laid out at LINESIZE (MAXDEC=2 here):

cat(res$listing, sep = "\n")
#> Change from baseline
#> 
#> The MEANS Procedure
#> 
#>                                      Analysis Variable : aval
#> 
#>                               N
#> arm                 week    Obs    N            Mean         Std Dev         Minimum         Maximum
#> ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
#> A                      0      2    2            9.90            0.42            9.60           10.20
#>                        4      2    2           11.95            0.21           11.80           12.10
#> B                      0      2    2           11.10            0.28           10.90           11.30
#>                        4      2    2           10.10            0.42            9.80           10.40
#> ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The HTML output

sas_html() writes the procedure output of a result as an HTML document: one table per ODS table, under the titles. The document embeds its style sheet (system.file("css", "sasonr.css", package = "sasonr")):

sas_html(res, file = "means.html")

sas_html(res, log = TRUE) adds the log after the tables. The HTML destination is open when a program starts; ODS HTML CLOSE; closes it (the tables of the following steps are left out of the document) and ODS HTML; opens it again.

BY groups

With a BY statement each BY group gets its own table under a BY line, in the listing and in the HTML document:

res_by <- sas_run("
data trial;
  input arm $ visit week aval;
  datalines;
A 1 0 10.2
A 1 4 11.8
A 2 0 9.6
A 2 4 12.1
B 1 0 10.9
B 1 4 10.4
B 2 0 11.3
B 2 4 9.8
;
run;
proc sort data=trial; by arm; run;
title 'Analysis value by arm';
proc means data=trial n mean maxdec=1;
  by arm;
  var aval;
run;
")
cat(res_by$listing, sep = "\n")
#> Analysis value by arm
#> 
#> 
#> arm=A
#> 
#> The MEANS Procedure
#> 
#> Analysis Variable : aval
#> 
#> N            Mean
#> -----------------
#> 4            10.9
#> -----------------
#> 
#> 
#> arm=B
#> 
#> Analysis Variable : aval
#> 
#> N            Mean
#> -----------------
#> 4            10.6
#> -----------------

The ODS tables

$ods holds the ODS tables of a result in output order. Each is a tibble of the raw values (numbers unformatted) with the table’s name, label, path, BY values and column headers as attributes:

tab <- res$ods[[1]]
attr(tab, "name")
#> [1] "Summary"
attr(tab, "path")
#> [1] "Means.Summary"
tab
#> <sasonr_ods_table> Summary (Summary statistics)
#>   path:     Means.Summary
#>   proc:     Means, template base.summary
#>   columns:
#>     arm [class]
#>     week [class]
#>     NObs [stat] "N Obs"
#>     aval_N [stat] "N"
#>     aval_Mean [stat] "Mean"
#>     aval_StdDev [stat] "Std Dev"
#>     aval_Min [stat] "Minimum"
#>     aval_Max [stat] "Maximum"
#>   header 1: Analysis Variable : aval 
#>   header 2: arm | week | N Obs | N | Mean | Std Dev | Minimum | Maximum
#>   rows:     4

ODS OUTPUT: the table as a data set

ODS OUTPUT Summary=<data set>; before the PROC MEANS step writes the Summary table to WORK, with the usual data set NOTE in the log:

res_out <- sas_run("
data trial;
  input arm $ aval;
  datalines;
A 10.2
A 11.8
B 10.9
B 10.4
;
run;
ods output Summary=stats;
proc means data=trial n mean;
  class arm;
  var aval;
run;
")
sas_log(res_out, echo = FALSE)
#> NOTE: The data set WORK.TRIAL has 4 observations and 2 variables.
#> NOTE: The data set WORK.STATS has 2 observations and 4 variables.
#> NOTE: There were 4 observations read from the data set WORK.TRIAL.
res_out$work$stats
#> # A tibble: 2 × 4
#>   arm    nobs aval_n aval_mean
#>   <chr> <dbl>  <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1 A         2      2      11  
#> 2 B         2      2      10.6

Procedures on data frames

sas_means_df(), sas_tabulate_df(), sas_freq_df() (one-way tables) and sas_transpose_df() run one procedure on a data frame without a program. They read their arguments with the same parser and specification builder as the PROC step of a program and call the same computation, so the table is the one the program gives. as.data.frame() drops the table attributes; sas_log() gives the WARNINGs and NOTEs of the computation and sas_html() the HTML document.

df <- data.frame(arm = c("A", "A", "B", "B"), aval = c(10.2, 11.8, 10.9, 10.4))
m <- sas_means_df(df, var = "aval", class = "arm", stats = c("n", "mean"))
as.data.frame(m)
#>   arm NObs aval_N aval_Mean
#> 1   A    2      2     11.00
#> 2   B    2      2     10.65
as.data.frame(sas_tabulate_df(df, "arm all, aval*(n mean)", class = "arm", var = "aval"))
#>    arm _C1_   _C2_
#> 1    A    2 11.000
#> 2    B    2 10.650
#> 3 <NA>    4 10.825
as.data.frame(sas_freq_df(df, "arm"))
#>   arm Frequency Percent CumFrequency CumPercent
#> 1   A         2      50            2         50
#> 2   B         2      50            4        100

The RTF document

ODS RTF FILE="path"; opens the RTF destination; the PROC PRINT and PROC TABULATE tables of the steps that follow go into the document, which is written at ODS RTF CLOSE;. The document follows the default RTF style: a heading row repeated on every page, row titles and headings in bold, merged row titles, BY lines, and the column widths of that style.

sas_run("
data trial;
  input arm $ aval;
  datalines;
A 10
B 11
;
run;
ods rtf file=\"trial.rtf\";
proc print data=trial;
run;
ods rtf close;
")

What fails loud

sasonr stops with a sasonr_unsupported condition, naming the SAS line, for output requests it does not implement: ODS HTML options other than FILE= and STYLE=HTMLBlue, ODS OUTPUT with MATCH_ALL, PERSIST= or BY groups, the ODS actions (CLOSE, SELECT, EXCLUDE, …), and FOOTNOTE statements in the HTML document. sas_html() also stops when the HTML destination received output that has no HTML view yet (PROC PRINT, PROC FREQ statistics other than CHISQ) (close the destination around those steps with ODS HTML CLOSE; to get the document of the others).
